title: Sicus: distinctive low-intervention wines from Catalunya
summary: Website: https://www.dynamicvines.com/producers/sicus I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of
content:
Website: https://www.dynamicvines.com/producers/sicus

I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of Sicus, an interesting winery based in Bonastre (near Tarrgona in Catalunya, Spain). It’s the project of Eduard Piè.

His focus is on indigenous varieties, organically grown and fermented in amphora (tinajas) made from local clay. Some of these are actually buried in the vineyards. Farming is organic, and the vineyards are no-till. Soils are limestone, and the vines are dry grown.

Sicus Pétillant Naturel A Wine Work Orange (S) 2021
Lively, tangy, bright with some savoury detail. Grippy and phenolic. Quite distinctive and delicious. Wild and structured gently fizzy. 90/100

Sicus Cartoixà Brisat (Orange) 2019
Xarel.lo is the grape variety here. This is bold, fresh, distinctive. Stony edge to the lively citrus fruit. Some orange peel. Bright and tangy with real energy. 94/100

Sicus Sumoi 2021
Single vineyard called ‘El Roldonar’, located at 185m high with a strong maritime influence. Silty soil of calcareous nature. Old vines. Whole bunch fermentation. 3 months in amphora, 5 months stainless steel. Nicely textured, some structure with good acidity too. Some warmth and texture to the cherry fruit. Just 10% alcohol. Nice savoury twist. Very distinctive with a drying finish. 93/100

Sicus Garrut 2019
Single vineyard called ‘La Obaga Del Gojo’, located at 220m with a strong maritime influence. Whole bunch. 2 months in amphora, 6 months in stainless steel. Rich, concentrated, savoury and intense with some grippy structure. Brooding and bold with firm tannins. Very gastronomic. Some texture and warmth. 92/100

title: Highlights: Roc des Anges Alquimia Vin de Voile NV Vin de France
summary: This is a blend of Grenache Gris and Macabeu from the amazing Roc des Anges in the Roussillon. It spends
content:
This is a blend of Grenache Gris and Macabeu from the amazing Roc des Anges in the Roussillon. It spends two and a half years in 228 litre barrels with no topping up. The name translates as ‘alchemist’ in Catalan.

Roc des Anges Alquimia Vin de Voile NV Vin de France
12.5% alcohol. Matured under a layer of flor in small oak barrels. This is complex with a subtle tangy flor character and a nice saltiness, as well as pear, peach and lemon fruit. There’s an innate richness to this wine, but it stays fresh and bright, with good acidity. Such a beautiful expression of the Roussillon, where the flor enhances and gives detail without dominating at all. 95/100

title: Germany’s top Rieslings at the VDP tasting: Mittelrhein, Franken, Sachsen, Nahe and Rheinhessen

content:
Continuing on my write ups from the VDP tastings in Wiesbaden, August 2026, here are the notes of Rieslings from Mittelrhein (just two), Sachsen (just one) and the more significant areas of Franken, Nahe and Rheinhessen. Some lovely wines here.

Mittelrhein

Ratzenberger Riesling Bacharach ST. JOST 2025 Mittelrhein
Nice core of sweet citrus fruit here with good balance and some riper pear and peach notes. 93/100

Ratzenberger Riesling Bacharach WOLFSHÖHLE 2025 Mittelrhein
Crisp, focused citrus fruit with nice acidity and freshness. Pure and primary. 93/100

Franken

Rudolf Fürst Riesling Bürgstadt CENTGRAFENBERG 2025 Franken
Honeyed, juicy and appealing with nice brightness to the lemony fruit. Zippy and quite mineral on the finish. Wide dynamic range. 94/100

Bürgerspital zum Hl. Geist Riesling Würzburg STEIN-BERG 2025 Franken
Juicy, bright and linear with nice acidity under the lively citrus fruit, with some chalky minerality. 94/100

Bürgerspital zum Hl. Geist Riesling Randersacker PFÜLBEN 2025 Franken
Compact and concentrated with a lovely mineral undertow to the bold citrus fruit. This is very stylish and intense. 95/100

Staatlicher Hofkeller Würzburg Riesling Randersacker PFÜLBEN 2025 Franken
Crisp, concentrated and layered, with bold lemony fruit and some nice mineral notes. Shows real intensity and depth with power and precision. Serious stuff. 95/100

Zehnthof Theo Luckert Riesling Sulzfeld MAUSTAL 2025 Franken
Intriguing nose with some smoky, herbal notes, leading to a midweight lemony palate that also has a lively finish. Such precision to this wine. 94/100

Rainer Sauer Riesling Escherndorf AM LUMPEN 1655® 2025 Franken
Beautifully focused, crystalline citrus fruit. Lemony and nicely taut with lovely detail on the finish. A lovely wine. 95/100

Horst Sauer Riesling Escherndorf AM LUMPEN 1655® 2025 Franken
Pristine and beautifull expressive with real precision to the bright lemony fruit. Zippy and detailed with nice intensity. Very stylish. 95/100

Max Müller I Riesling Escherndorf AM LUMPEN 1655® 2025 Franken
A rich, ripe, dense fruity style with lemon and pear as well as some peach, but it still has good acidity. 93/100

Max Müller I Riesling Volkach RATSHERR 2025 Franken
Chalky, lemony nose leads to a bright, focused palate showing keen acidity and nice weight. Stylish. 93/100

Höfler Riesling Michelbach APOSTELGARTEN 2024 Franken
This is compact and slightly salty with bold citrus fruit and a slightly pithy edge. 92/100Am Stein-Ludwig Knoll Riesling Stetten STEIN 2024 Franken
Juicy and slightly pithy with compact lemony fruit. Nice brightness to this wine. 93/100

Sachsen

Martin Schwarz Riesling Radebeul FRIEDSTEIN 2024 Sachsen
There’s a slightly smoky undertow to this layered, textural Riesling with bright citrus fruit dominating. 92/100

Nahe

Schäfer-Fröhlich Riesling Monzingen FRÜHLINGSPLÄTZCHEN 2025 Nahe
Smoky, mineral, crystalline nose. The palate is concentrated and energetic with bright lemony fruit. Pretty and expressive. 94/100

Emrich-Schönleber Riesling Monzingen FRÜHLINGSPLÄTZCHEN 2025 Nahe
Juicy and linear with expressive lemony fruit. Zesty and refreshing. Midweight in style. 93/100

Emrich-Schönleber Riesling Monzingen HALENBERG 2025 Nahe
Nice focus and precision here with delicate lemony fruit and lovely aromatics. Midweight in style. 93/100

Schäfer-Fröhlich Riesling Monzingen HALENBERG 2025 Nahe
Nice tension and balance with crystalline citrus fruit, a touch of fruit sweetness, and really expressive character. Balanced. 94/100

Schäfer-Fröhlich Riesling Bockenau FELSENECK 2025 Nahe
Zippy and slightly stony. Midweight citrus fruit, with an expressive personality. Some delicacy and poise here. 93/100

Schäfer-Fröhlich Riesling Bockenau STROMBERG 2025 Nahe     
Compact, pithy and slightly smoky with a nice delicacy on the mid-palate, showing pure lemony fruit. 93/100

Dr. Crusius Riesling Schlossböckelheim FELSENBERG 2025 Nahe
Delicate and fine with lovely focused citrus fruit. A lighter style but with nice tension. 93/100

Gut Hermannsberg Riesling Schlossböckelheim FELSENBERG 2025 Nahe
There’s a touch of richness with ripe citrus fruit, but also nice delicacy and balance. Midweight but with nice finesse. 94/100

H. Dönnhoff Riesling Schlossböckelheim FELSENBERG 2025 Nahe
Chiselled, crystalline and focused with a core of sweet citrus fruit. Nice energy and brightness here with freshness and tension. So stylish. 95/100

Schäfer-Fröhlich Riesling Schlossböckelheim FELSENBERG 2025 Nahe
Slightly reductive nose with wet stone minerality. The palate is compact and bright with some grip. Juicy. 92/100

Dr. Crusius Riesling Schlossböckelheim KUPFERGRUBE 2025 Nahe
Fresh and textured with nice weight. Citrus and some pear. There’s a nice fruit focus. 92/100

Schäfer-Fröhlich Riesling Schlossböckelheim KUPFERGRUBE 2025 Nahe
Compact and pithy and quite angular with a savoury twist to the citrus fruit. Unfurled. 91/100

Gut Hermannsberg Riesling Niederhausen STEINBERG 2025 Nahe
Nice flesh here with ripe pear and citrus fruit. Still primary, with nice fruit depth and some mineral undertow. 94/100

H. Dönnhoff Riesling Niederhausen HERMANNSHÖHLE 2025 Nahe
Beautiful layered, taut citrus fruit with some floral aromatics, and a nuanced, mid-weight palate with real beauty. 94/100

Gut Hermannsberg Riesling Niederhausen IN DER ROSSEL 2025 Nahe
Fleshy with a hint of apricot richness as well as ripe pear and citrus fruit. Nice generosity and poise here. 94/100

H. Dönnhoff Riesling Norheim DELLCHEN 2025 Nahe
Crystalline, delicate and well defined with nice expressive citrus fruit. Not heavy or bold, just delicate and expressive. 95/100

Dr. Crusius Riesling Traisen BASTEI 2025 Nahe
Lovely compact, crystalline citrus fruit with good density and a tapering, elegant finish. 93/100

Gut Hermannsberg Riesling Altenbamberg ROTENBERG 2025 Nahe
Lovely fruit purity here. Ripe lemony fruit with good density and focus. This is bright and expressive showing good weight and some delicate fruitiness on the finish. 94/100

H. Dönnhoff Riesling Kreuznach KRÖTENPFUHL 2025 Nahe
Lively, bright, nuanced. Nice crystalline citrus fruit with good acidity. Some tension here. 94/100

H. Dönnhoff Riesling Roxheim IM MÜHLENBERG 2025 Nahe
Delicate, juicy and focused with a core of sweet citrus fruit. Nice purity and energy. Not heavy, more mid-weight. 93/100

Joh. Bapt. Schäfer Riesling Dorsheim PITTERMÄNNCHEN 2025 Nahe
Compact citrus fruit. Pretty, stony, linear. 93/100

Joh. Bapt. Schäfer Riesling Dorsheim GOLDLOCH 2025 Nahe
Crisp and nicely weighted with nice purity and energy. Shows appealing fruit with good presence. 92/100

Kruger-Rumpf Riesling Dorsheim BURGBERG 2025 Nahe
Nice weight here with good freshness and balance to the crisp citrus fruit. 93/100

Kruger-Rumpf Riesling Münster IM PITTERBERG 2025 Nahe
Nice ripe, sweet citrus fruit with some generosity and good weight. Nicely poised and focused. Pleasurable. 94/100

Kruger-Rumpf Riesling Münster DAUTENPFLÄNZER 2025 Nahe
Bright, crystalline and quite energetic with lovely taut citrus fruit. Nicely dense with good supporting acidity. 93/100

Schlossgut Diel Riesling Dorsheim PITTERMÄNNCHEN 2024 Nahe
Lean, stony and mineral with focused lemony fruit framed by brisk acidity. 93/100

Schlossgut Diel Riesling Dorsheim GOLDLOCH 2024 Nahe
Crisp, juicy and linear with taut, almost lean lemony fruit, finishing long but tight. 94/100

Schlossgut Diel Riesling Dorsheim BURGBERG 2024 Nahe
Chiselled, taut and focused with real purity and restraint, and good acidity. Primary, but with potential. Quite lean. 94/100

Gut Hermannsberg Riesling Schlossböckelheim KUPFERGRUBE 2021 Nahe
Bright but fleshy with generous citrus fruit and a touch of peachy richness, finishing long and tapering with good acidity. 94/100

Gut Hermannsberg Riesling Niederhausen HERMANNSBERG 2021 Nahe
Stony, juicy and vivid with nice tension to the pear and citrus fruit. Good energy here with some brightness. Nice ripeness to the fruit, showing potential for development. 95/100

Rheinhessen

Bischel Riesling Bingen SCHARLACHBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Lively and bright with nice zippy lemony fruit. Juicy and quite intense with good acidity. Lean style, zippy and racy. 93/100

Kruger-Rumpf Riesling Bingen SCHARLACHBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Zippy, racy and pure with keen acidity and a sort of transparency. Citrus fruit dominated, but not overly fruity. Mineral and brisk. 94/100

Wagner-Stempel Riesling Bingen SCHARLACHBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Juicy and energetic with keen mineral-laced lemony fruit supported by good acidity. Such precision here. 94/100

Bischel Riesling Appenheim HUNDERTGULDEN 2025 Rheinhessen
Juicy, bright and focused. Some smoky minerality, and high acidity. Searing and intense with good depth of flavour. 94/100

Knewitz Riesling Appenheim HUNDERTGULDEN 2025 Rheinhessen
Pure, bright and linear with nice tension to the fruit. Has an expressive personality. Great balance here. Sp pure and fine. 95/100

Knewitz Riesling Nieder-Hilbersheim HONIGBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Nice texture and weight to this Riesling, which shows lovely balance and purity. Lots of fruit, but also tension and minerality. 94/100

Knewitz Riesling Nieder-Hilbersheim STEINACKER 2025 Rheinhessen
Chiselled, pure and bright but also showing good depth of citrus fruit, with some peachy richness. But it stays linear and focused, and finishes fine and long. 95/100

Bischel Riesling Siefersheim HEERKRETZ 2025 Rheinhessen
Juicy and quite taut, but with some peachy richness as well as the crystalline citrus fruit, as well as some saltiness on the finish. Very fine. 94/100

Wagner-Stempel Riesling Siefersheim HEERKRETZ 2025 Rheinhessen
A great marriage of precision with some depth, showing crystalline citrus fruits backed by nice acidity. So stylish and refined. 95/100

Gunderloch Riesling Nackenheim ROTHENBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Bright, perfumed and refined with juicy lemony fruit and some nice salty minerality. Has some nice spicy character here as well as chiselled fruit. 94/100

Kühling-Gillot Riesling Nackenheim ROTHENBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Some nice ripe citrus fruit here, a touch of melony richness, and then nice layered acidity. Real finesse and purity, with a spicy fringe. 94/100

Gunderloch Riesling Nierstein PETTENTHAL 2025 Rheinhessen
Nice tension here with bright lemony fruit and some mineral undertow. Compact fruit but there’s some generosity as well. 93/100

Kühling-Gillot Riesling Nierstein PETTENTHAL 2025 Rheinhessen
Textured and refined with a fine spicy detail to the generous citrus fruit. This has nice ripe fruit. 94/100

Rappenhof Riesling Nierstein PETTENTHAL 2025 Rheinhessen
Zippy lemony fruit with good acidity, but also some fine spicy structure. Bright and refined. 94/100

Gunderloch Riesling Nierstein HIPPING 2025 Rheinhessen
Chalky and grainy structure here under the ripe but textured lemony fruit. Lovely mineral finish that tapers nicely. Saline twist. 95/100

Kühling-Gillot Riesling Nierstein HIPPING 2025 Rheinhessen

Kühling-Gillot Riesling Nierstein ÖLBERG 2025 Rheinhessen

Rappenhof Riesling Nierstein ÖLBERG 2025 Rheinhessen
Nice tension and intensity to this wine with keen acidity behind the pure citrus fruit. Crisp and juicy with nice weight in the mouth. 94/100

Rappenhof Riesling Oppenheim HERRENBERG 2025 Rheinhessen

Rappenhof Riesling Oppenheim SACKTRÄGER 2025 Rheinhessen

Battenfeld Spanier Riesling Hohen-Sülzen KIRCHENSTÜCK 2025 Rheinhessen

Textural and refined with attractive lemon and pear fruit, showing nice density and focus. Crystalline finish. Quite fine. 95/100

title: Highlights: an amazing vinous cider from Little Pomona

content:
Website: https://littlepomona.com/pages/about-us

I’m going slightly off-message and including a cider here. It’s from the excellent Little Pomona, and it was inspired by the wines of the Jura. It’s made from the Egremont Russet apple variety, wild-fermented in oak and flor-aged for three years. Superb.

Little Pomona Many Rivers Egremont Russet Flor Aged Yellow Cider 2022
7.7% alcohol. Egremont Russet, wild-fermented in oak and flor-aged for three years. Some ripe apple on the nose, but also crystalline citrus and a whiff of the seashore. In the mouth this has a lovely spicy, mineral savouriness. Vinous with some structure to the fruit. Very stylish and layered, with nice grip and a tangy, lemony twist. This is quite beautiful. 9/10 (£16 direct from producer)

summary: It’s the penultimate day of harvest at Oxfordshire winery Hundred Hills. They are picking Pinot Noir for the famed Rosé
content: It’s the penultimate day of harvest at Oxfordshire winery Hundred Hills. They are picking Pinot Noir for the famed Rosé de Saignée cuvée, which is made by macerating destemmed grapes on skins and then pressing to barrel when the colour is right. We tasted the 2022 release and then juice with different periods of skin contact from the 2026 vintage.

title: Highlights: Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
summary: A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria. Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking
content:
A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria.

Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking project an Australian couple, James Hird and Annie Conley. Hird was co-founder of Sydney’s Rootstock natural wine festival, and Conley was a food and travel writer. They relocated to Umbria to purchase Beulah Violetta, an 150-year-old estate near Todi. Embracing regenerative and certified-biodynamic farming, they manage ten hectares of vines, olive groves, and wheat fields. This is a blend of Merlot, Sangiovese and Sagrantino, fermented in stainless steel, with low sulfite additions. Lovely vivid floral berry, cherry and plum fruit on the nose. The palate is pure and fresh with nicely proportioned raspberry and cherry fruit with some spiciness and a supple green note. Such lovely generosity of fruit, with a bit of savoury grip. Liquorice and a hint of tar. 92/100 (UK agent Les Caves de Pyrene, retail typically £20.50 in independents)

title: Highlights: Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024 Ceres, South Africa
summary: Impressed by this Pinot from a region in South Africa that isn’t well known for it. Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024
content:
Impressed by this Pinot from a region in South Africa that isn’t well known for it.

Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024 Ceres, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is a really interesting expression of Pinot Noir, from Ceres, which is an elevated plateau (700-100 m) inland, just above Worcester and immediately east of Tulbach. It reminds me a bit of an elegant Nebbiolo, rather than Pinot, but that’s probably the terroir speaking. Fresh, aromatic and taut on the nose with redcurrant and bloody notes, as well as some red cherry. The palate has elegance and freshness with tapering red cherry and redcurrant fruit, as well as some fine spice, showing good acidity but also some grippy, yet refined tannin. There’s a slight drying on the finish which makes me think of Nebbiolo. Such a lovely expression of Pinot Noir with a point of difference. Great work from Cerina van Niekerk. 94/100 (£27.50 Stone Vine and Sun)

title: Notes from a remarkable long lunch at Gaveto in Matosinhos, Portugal, with Niepoort, Transmission and friends, plus some amazing Champagnes
summary: As far as lunches go, this was one of the best I’ve had in recent years, held at the remarkable
content:
As far as lunches go, this was one of the best I’ve had in recent years, held at the remarkable Gaveto restaurant in Matosinhos, the port area in Porto. Great people, memorable wines, a relaxed vibe. The food, as always, was spot on.

Champagne Remi Leroy Blanc de Quatre Cépages Mer Sur Mont 2016 France
Complex, layered and powerful with a citrus drive and subtle toast and spice notes. Really vinous with a saline edge to it. Real energy here: so expressive, with such precision. 95/100

Transmission Sparkling NV Bairrada, Portugal
This is a blend of 20/21/22/23 vintages. Lively and intense with powerful citrus fruit with some lime note. Good structure, really vital. 93/100

Niepoort Charme 2005 Douro, Portugal
Elegant, fine and textural with some spicy detail. Has some cherry and raspberry fruit still with a hint of earthy spicy development. This is in a beautiful place. It has density richness and elegance. 95/100

Niepoort Charme 2012 Douro, Portugal
Such focus and elegance here: very fine and expressive with some mineral intensity and a spicy underlay to the concentrated fruit. Still structured. Give this wine time. 96/100

Niepoort Charme 2018 Douro, Portugal
This has presence and elegance with a core of sweet cherry and berry fruit. Such elegance and poise. There’s a little development, but there’s structure and precision to the red cherry and berry fruits. 96/100

Niepoort Projectos Bastardo 2021 Douro, Portugal
Floral and expressive with sappy green nose to the lovely sweet strawberry and spice palate. This has lovely texture and a core of sweet fruit. Quite Cinsualt-like with a grippy grippy spicy finish. 94/100

Niepoort Museu dos Lagares 2022 Douro, Portugal
Very pale in colour. Supple, elegant and very fine, with nice structure and real tension . This is beautifully transparent but with some density, showing real finesse. 96/100

Niepoort Vinha do Carril 2023 Douro, Portugal
Vivid red colour. Fine, tight, linear and expressive with raspberry and redcurrant fruit showing real finesse, and just a touch of reduction. So elegant and linear with real precision. 97/100

Champagne Adrian Renoir Les Vignes Goisses Grand Cru Verzy Pinot Meunier 2019 France
Complex and layered with real intensity and nice structure, showing saline complexity. Bold with good structure, and a lovely orange peel and grapefruit edge, as well as appealing salinity. 96/100

Transmission Branco 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (sample)
Fine lively and expressive with lovely energy. Quite layered and mineral with some sweet citrus, as well as real precision. Combines some fruit sweetness with mineral density. 95/100

Transmission Tinto 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (sample)
Supple elegance and refined with red cherry, iodine and redcurrant notes. Lovely precision but also some depth. Very fine with a subtle spiciness. Potentially brilliant. 97/100

Transmission Blanco 2020 Bairrada, Portugal
This is in a beautiful place now. Complex, waxy and mineral with a fine salty edge, starting to develop real complexity. Good intensity. So exciting and multi-layered. 97/100

Niepoort Coche 2024 Douro, Portugal
We tried this blind. Interesting reduction on the nose: mineral, spicy, fresh and citrussy. The palate is supple and elegant with ripe pear and some peach. Very textural and mineral, showing such finesse. Profound. 96/100

Daganeau Blanc Fumé de Pouilly Silex 2001 Loire, France
12.5% alcohol. Powerful, textured and broad with melon and pear fruit as well as some peach and apricot, coupled with some lovely green hints. Such precision and purity here this, with crushed rock minerality. Really complex. 96/100

Niepoort Redoma Branco 1996 Douro, Portugal
Toast, honey, spice and wax on the nose. Lovely precision with some richness and very fine toasty development. This shows crystalline citrus fruit and nice depth, and it is still fresh. 94/100

Gonçalves Faria Blanco 2017 Bairadda, Portugal
Tasted blind. Complex toast, spice and iodine notes as well as salty citrus notes. Lovely depth and complexity. There’s real concentration here, and some age to this wine. Good intensity and depth with real precision and focus. 95/100

Niepoort Vinha Limena 2021 Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
This is simple and fresh with raspberry red cherry fruit and some real elegance. Very pure with depth under the sweet cherries, strawberries and raspberries. Amazing elegance for the Alentejo. 95/100

Sidecar NV (2018/2019) Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
Made by Ricardo Freitas and Susana Esteban. Ripe, sweet and supple with sweet raspberry and cherry fruit, as well as a hint of liquorice. Such focus, brightness and elegance. 94/100

Champagne Cédric Bouchard Roses de Jeanne UR/R19 Dégorgement 2023 France
Bright, fresh and linear with nice crystalline citrus fruit. Such purity with linear citrus fruit. Concentrated, pure and well detailed with real finesse as well as intensity. 95/100

Niepoort Vintage Port 2024 Douro, Portugal
Concentrated and refined, and also structured, with lovely blueberry and black cherry fruit as well as some blackcurrant. Real density and intensity, with structure, focus and amazing concentration. 96/100

Barbeito 50 Year Old Verdelho NV Madeira
This is amazing. Rich, complex, spicy and intense, with old wood spice, tar and mineral notes showing real finesse. Amazing depth and complexity. 96/100

Champagne Dom Pérignon P3 1992 France
Going back in time with this. Toast, spice, crystalline citrus, orange peel and lime notes. Lovely structure with great acidity. Mineral and spicy. Such harmony, and a warm spicy finish. 96/100

Champagne Krug Edition 173 NV France
Lovely intensity here. Vivid and crystalline, with fresh lime, lemon, spice and toast notes, showing real precision. 96/100

title: Going to the football? Like good wine? A tasting trip through Islington’s wine bars pairs well with tickets for a north London matchday
summary: There’s something special about the occasion when it comes to attending a football match, especially if you really care about
content:
There’s something special about the occasion when it comes to attending a football match, especially if you really care about the outcome. Part of the appeal is that victory is not guaranteed. You might spend money and time watching a game that ends in a stale 0-0 draw, or you might see your team put up a poor display and get beaten. But when it’s a good game, and your team wins, there’s nothing quite like it. But a football match is more than just attending a game. It’s the stuff around the 90 minutes of action that makes it a great day out, including some pre-game or post-game drinks, and perhaps a meal, too.

Beer is the drink most closely associated with football, but if you want to do more than swill a few pre-match pints (nothing wrong with that of course), what about tasting some interesting wines. And if you are heading to a match at Highbury, there are some great wine bar options in the Islington area that are worth a detour. A tasting trip through Islington’s wine bars pairs neatly with tickets for a north London matchday when the fixture falls right.

My favourite is more than just a wine bar, and more than just a pub. The Draper’s Arms is an Islington institution and has one of the best wine lists in London in terms of its diversity, and also its fair pricing. You can come here and eat very well, but you can also come here just to share a couple of bottles of excellent wine. It has a beautiful blue façade, and inside it’s accommodating and warm with a spacious dining room and a classy feel to the bar area. Highly recommended.

I also have a soft spot for Yield, a small but perfectly formed wine bar specializing in low-intervention/natural wines. There’s a really inviting, relaxed feel to this bar, and the wines are attractively priced. You just want to stay and drink another bottle.

Close to Yield is Trullo, which isn’t a wine bar, although it does have an excellent wine list. Trullo can rightfully claim to be one of London’s very best Italian restaurants, and it’s the ideal place to eat, before or after the game, although reservations here are essential. Seats here are rightfully in high demand.

title: Sicus: distinctive low-intervention wines from Catalunya
summary: Website: https://www.dynamicvines.com/producers/sicus I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of
content:
Website: https://www.dynamicvines.com/producers/sicus

I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of Sicus, an interesting winery based in Bonastre (near Tarrgona in Catalunya, Spain). It’s the project of Eduard Piè.

His focus is on indigenous varieties, organically grown and fermented in amphora (tinajas) made from local clay. Some of these are actually buried in the vineyards. Farming is organic, and the vineyards are no-till. Soils are limestone, and the vines are dry grown.

Sicus Pétillant Naturel A Wine Work Orange (S) 2021
Lively, tangy, bright with some savoury detail. Grippy and phenolic. Quite distinctive and delicious. Wild and structured gently fizzy. 90/100

Sicus Cartoixà Brisat (Orange) 2019
Xarel.lo is the grape variety here. This is bold, fresh, distinctive. Stony edge to the lively citrus fruit. Some orange peel. Bright and tangy with real energy. 94/100

Sicus Sumoi 2021
Single vineyard called ‘El Roldonar’, located at 185m high with a strong maritime influence. Silty soil of calcareous nature. Old vines. Whole bunch fermentation. 3 months in amphora, 5 months stainless steel. Nicely textured, some structure with good acidity too. Some warmth and texture to the cherry fruit. Just 10% alcohol. Nice savoury twist. Very distinctive with a drying finish. 93/100

Sicus Garrut 2019
Single vineyard called ‘La Obaga Del Gojo’, located at 220m with a strong maritime influence. Whole bunch. 2 months in amphora, 6 months in stainless steel. Rich, concentrated, savoury and intense with some grippy structure. Brooding and bold with firm tannins. Very gastronomic. Some texture and warmth. 92/100

title: Highlights: Roc des Anges Alquimia Vin de Voile NV Vin de France

content:
This is a blend of Grenache Gris and Macabeu from the amazing Roc des Anges in the Roussillon. It spends two and a half years in 228 litre barrels with no topping up. The name translates as ‘alchemist’ in Catalan.

Roc des Anges Alquimia Vin de Voile NV Vin de France
12.5% alcohol. Matured under a layer of flor in small oak barrels. This is complex with a subtle tangy flor character and a nice saltiness, as well as pear, peach and lemon fruit. There’s an innate richness to this wine, but it stays fresh and bright, with good acidity. Such a beautiful expression of the Roussillon, where the flor enhances and gives detail without dominating at all. 95/100

title: Highlights: Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
summary: A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria. Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking
content:
A lovely low-intervention red from Umbria.

Stesso Stesso Beulah Violetta Rosso 2024 Umbria, Italy
12.5% alcohol. Stesso Stesso is the winemaking project an Australian couple, James Hird and Annie Conley. Hird was co-founder of Sydney’s Rootstock natural wine festival, and Conley was a food and travel writer. They relocated to Umbria to purchase Beulah Violetta, an 150-year-old estate near Todi. Embracing regenerative and certified-biodynamic farming, they manage ten hectares of vines, olive groves, and wheat fields. This is a blend of Merlot, Sangiovese and Sagrantino, fermented in stainless steel, with low sulfite additions. Lovely vivid floral berry, cherry and plum fruit on the nose. The palate is pure and fresh with nicely proportioned raspberry and cherry fruit with some spiciness and a supple green note. Such lovely generosity of fruit, with a bit of savoury grip. Liquorice and a hint of tar. 92/100 (UK agent Les Caves de Pyrene, retail typically £20.50 in independents)

title: Highlights: Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024 Ceres, South Africa

content:
Impressed by this Pinot from a region in South Africa that isn’t well known for it.

Cecilia Pinot Noir 2024 Ceres, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is a really interesting expression of Pinot Noir, from Ceres, which is an elevated plateau (700-100 m) inland, just above Worcester and immediately east of Tulbach. It reminds me a bit of an elegant Nebbiolo, rather than Pinot, but that’s probably the terroir speaking. Fresh, aromatic and taut on the nose with redcurrant and bloody notes, as well as some red cherry. The palate has elegance and freshness with tapering red cherry and redcurrant fruit, as well as some fine spice, showing good acidity but also some grippy, yet refined tannin. There’s a slight drying on the finish which makes me think of Nebbiolo. Such a lovely expression of Pinot Noir with a point of difference. Great work from Cerina van Niekerk. 94/100 (£27.50 Stone Vine and Sun)

title: Notes from a remarkable long lunch at Gaveto in Matosinhos, Portugal, with Niepoort, Transmission and friends, plus some amazing Champagnes

content:
As far as lunches go, this was one of the best I’ve had in recent years, held at the remarkable Gaveto restaurant in Matosinhos, the port area in Porto. Great people, memorable wines, a relaxed vibe. The food, as always, was spot on.

Champagne Remi Leroy Blanc de Quatre Cépages Mer Sur Mont 2016 France
Complex, layered and powerful with a citrus drive and subtle toast and spice notes. Really vinous with a saline edge to it. Real energy here: so expressive, with such precision. 95/100

Transmission Sparkling NV Bairrada, Portugal
This is a blend of 20/21/22/23 vintages. Lively and intense with powerful citrus fruit with some lime note. Good structure, really vital. 93/100

Niepoort Charme 2005 Douro, Portugal
Elegant, fine and textural with some spicy detail. Has some cherry and raspberry fruit still with a hint of earthy spicy development. This is in a beautiful place. It has density richness and elegance. 95/100

Niepoort Charme 2012 Douro, Portugal
Such focus and elegance here: very fine and expressive with some mineral intensity and a spicy underlay to the concentrated fruit. Still structured. Give this wine time. 96/100

Niepoort Charme 2018 Douro, Portugal
This has presence and elegance with a core of sweet cherry and berry fruit. Such elegance and poise. There’s a little development, but there’s structure and precision to the red cherry and berry fruits. 96/100

Niepoort Projectos Bastardo 2021 Douro, Portugal
Floral and expressive with sappy green nose to the lovely sweet strawberry and spice palate. This has lovely texture and a core of sweet fruit. Quite Cinsualt-like with a grippy grippy spicy finish. 94/100

Niepoort Museu dos Lagares 2022 Douro, Portugal
Very pale in colour. Supple, elegant and very fine, with nice structure and real tension . This is beautifully transparent but with some density, showing real finesse. 96/100

Niepoort Vinha do Carril 2023 Douro, Portugal
Vivid red colour. Fine, tight, linear and expressive with raspberry and redcurrant fruit showing real finesse, and just a touch of reduction. So elegant and linear with real precision. 97/100

Champagne Adrian Renoir Les Vignes Goisses Grand Cru Verzy Pinot Meunier 2019 France
Complex and layered with real intensity and nice structure, showing saline complexity. Bold with good structure, and a lovely orange peel and grapefruit edge, as well as appealing salinity. 96/100

Transmission Branco 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (sample)
Fine lively and expressive with lovely energy. Quite layered and mineral with some sweet citrus, as well as real precision. Combines some fruit sweetness with mineral density. 95/100

Transmission Tinto 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (sample)
Supple elegance and refined with red cherry, iodine and redcurrant notes. Lovely precision but also some depth. Very fine with a subtle spiciness. Potentially brilliant. 97/100

Transmission Blanco 2020 Bairrada, Portugal
This is in a beautiful place now. Complex, waxy and mineral with a fine salty edge, starting to develop real complexity. Good intensity. So exciting and multi-layered. 97/100

Niepoort Coche 2024 Douro, Portugal
We tried this blind. Interesting reduction on the nose: mineral, spicy, fresh and citrussy. The palate is supple and elegant with ripe pear and some peach. Very textural and mineral, showing such finesse. Profound. 96/100

12.5% alcohol. Powerful, textured and broad with melon and pear fruit as well as some peach and apricot, coupled with some lovely green hints. Such precision and purity here this, with crushed rock minerality. Really complex. 96/100

Niepoort Redoma Branco 1996 Douro, Portugal
Toast, honey, spice and wax on the nose. Lovely precision with some richness and very fine toasty development. This shows crystalline citrus fruit and nice depth, and it is still fresh. 94/100

Gonçalves Faria Blanco 2017 Bairadda, Portugal
Tasted blind. Complex toast, spice and iodine notes as well as salty citrus notes. Lovely depth and complexity. There’s real concentration here, and some age to this wine. Good intensity and depth with real precision and focus. 95/100

Niepoort Vinha Limena 2021 Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
This is simple and fresh with raspberry red cherry fruit and some real elegance. Very pure with depth under the sweet cherries, strawberries and raspberries. Amazing elegance for the Alentejo. 95/100

Sidecar NV (2018/2019) Portalegre, Alentejo, Portugal
Made by Ricardo Freitas and Susana Esteban. Ripe, sweet and supple with sweet raspberry and cherry fruit, as well as a hint of liquorice. Such focus, brightness and elegance. 94/100

Champagne Cédric Bouchard Roses de Jeanne UR/R19 Dégorgement 2023 France
Bright, fresh and linear with nice crystalline citrus fruit. Such purity with linear citrus fruit. Concentrated, pure and well detailed with real finesse as well as intensity. 95/100

Niepoort Vintage Port 2024 Douro, Portugal
Concentrated and refined, and also structured, with lovely blueberry and black cherry fruit as well as some blackcurrant. Real density and intensity, with structure, focus and amazing concentration. 96/100

Barbeito 50 Year Old Verdelho NV Madeira
This is amazing. Rich, complex, spicy and intense, with old wood spice, tar and mineral notes showing real finesse. Amazing depth and complexity. 96/100

Champagne Dom Pérignon P3 1992 France
Going back in time with this. Toast, spice, crystalline citrus, orange peel and lime notes. Lovely structure with great acidity. Mineral and spicy. Such harmony, and a warm spicy finish. 96/100

Champagne Krug Edition 173 NV France
Lovely intensity here. Vivid and crystalline, with fresh lime, lemon, spice and toast notes, showing real precision. 96/100

title: Going to the football? Like good wine? A tasting trip through Islington’s wine bars pairs well with tickets for a north London matchday
summary: There’s something special about the occasion when it comes to attending a football match, especially if you really care about
content:
There’s something special about the occasion when it comes to attending a football match, especially if you really care about the outcome. Part of the appeal is that victory is not guaranteed. You might spend money and time watching a game that ends in a stale 0-0 draw, or you might see your team put up a poor display and get beaten. But when it’s a good game, and your team wins, there’s nothing quite like it. But a football match is more than just attending a game. It’s the stuff around the 90 minutes of action that makes it a great day out, including some pre-game or post-game drinks, and perhaps a meal, too.

Beer is the drink most closely associated with football, but if you want to do more than swill a few pre-match pints (nothing wrong with that of course), what about tasting some interesting wines. And if you are heading to a match at Highbury, there are some great wine bar options in the Islington area that are worth a detour. A tasting trip through Islington’s wine bars pairs neatly with tickets for a north London matchday when the fixture falls right.

My favourite is more than just a wine bar, and more than just a pub. The Draper’s Arms is an Islington institution and has one of the best wine lists in London in terms of its diversity, and also its fair pricing. You can come here and eat very well, but you can also come here just to share a couple of bottles of excellent wine. It has a beautiful blue façade, and inside it’s accommodating and warm with a spacious dining room and a classy feel to the bar area. Highly recommended.

I also have a soft spot for Yield, a small but perfectly formed wine bar specializing in low-intervention/natural wines. There’s a really inviting, relaxed feel to this bar, and the wines are attractively priced. You just want to stay and drink another bottle.

Close to Yield is Trullo, which isn’t a wine bar, although it does have an excellent wine list. Trullo can rightfully claim to be one of London’s very best Italian restaurants, and it’s the ideal place to eat, before or after the game, although reservations here are essential. Seats here are rightfully in high demand.

And another good Islington choice is Humble Grape, which is a large wine bar and kitchen with an impressive selection of wines. This veers away from the natural to a more conventional list, but there are lots of good choices here.
